messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — I noticed a tenant triggering repeated alerts (5-10/min) on a noisy SLO; it's creating page storms across multiple oncallers. Thinking about adding a routing-level circuit breaker that temporarily suppresses notify fanout after a threshold. Want to align on API shape and console UX before we prototype.
Kevin Ortiz: +1 for suppression but prefer token-bucket/leaky-bucket style so we dampen instead of hard-cut. Allows short bursts to pass but protects from sustained spam.
Anya Patel: UX question — how do we present this in Console? Options: per-tenant toggle, SLO-linked recommendation, or an opt-in "suggested quiet window" modal when we detect flapping? Also we need clear copy so teams understand suppression vs. SLO state.
Samir Rao: API note: we already evaluate notify_policy -> routes -> thresholds. Adding a circuit_breaker key is fine but we must avoid exploding evaluation paths. Maybe make it a separate linked policy (signal_policy) referenced by SLO id to keep backwards compatibility.
Maria Chen: linking as a separate signal_policy sounds safer. Console could list a suggested signal_policy with one-click apply and explainers.
Kevin Ortiz: Important: when suppressing we must still emit telemetry like suppressed_count and last_unsuppressed_sample. Otherwise we blind operators and analytics. Also tag suppressed events with the reason.
Anya Patel: UI wireframe idea: on the SLO details page show an "Auto-quiet suggestions" card with a preview: estimated pages avoided, expected reduction %, and a dry-run toggle. Also show a timeline overlay of suppression intervals.
Maria Chen: metrics to expose: alert_rate (raw), suppressed_rate, suppression_duration_histogram, last_suppressed_at, and attempted_fallbacks (email/slack/pager). These help oncall decide if suppression hid important signals.
Samir Rao: rough contract sketch:
```
signal_policy:
  id: "sp-..."
  linked_slo_id: "slo-..."
  mode: "token_bucket" # or "binary"
  rate_limit_per_min: 30
  burst: 60
  backoff_window_seconds: 600
  emit_metrics: ["suppressed_count","suppressed_reason"]
```
We should default emit_metrics=false for privacy but allow teams to opt-in.
Kevin Ortiz: Also include suppression_reason tags (e.g., "noisy-signal-protection", "tenant-spillover") so downstream analytics can reconstruct decisions and do root-cause.
Anya Patel: Console timeline: grey bands for suppression, with hover details (start/end, reason, pages avoided). Also a CTA to run a dry-run simulation across selected time range.
Maria Chen: rollout plan: 1) suggestion-only read mode in staging for a couple tenants, with generated estimates and dry-run sim; 2) opt-in suppression behind feature flag for a pilot; 3) gradual enable with monitoring and automatic rollback if false-negative ratio exceeds threshold. No automatic suppression without human opt-in for first month.
deploy-bot: feature-flag update: feature "slo-suppression-protector" enabled in staging for 3 tenants.
Samir Rao: ops question: how to backfill suppressed_count historically? Need simulation mode in the evaluation engine to replay sampled signals over a window. We can reuse the eval sampling pipeline.
Kevin Ortiz: keep simulations lightweight: run against sampled signals and use approximation for high-volume tenants. Also expose confidence interval on pages-avoided estimate.
Anya Patel: product ask: add a prominent "run dry-run" CTA in the suggestion card and a short explainer modal (what suppression does, what metrics are retained).
Maria Chen: I'll draft an RFC that includes API contract, console mocks, telemetry schema, and rollout checklist. Volunteers?
Kevin Ortiz: I'll owner the sampling/engine feasibility and simulation infra.
Samir Rao: I'll own API compatibility, eval sim, and telemetry hooks.
Anya Patel: I'll produce UI mocks and the copy for explainers.
Maria Chen: Thanks — can we aim to ship RFC by EOD Thursday? :thumbsup:
